findings.title: canManage() grants manage access when caller only has VIEW permission
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` checks `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` instead of only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (and the Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` documents this same check). Because `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` (`POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups`) calls `auth.groups().requireManage()`, any admin granted only the `view` scope on the `Groups` resource type will pass `requireManage()` and be able to create new top-level groups or move existing subgroups to top-level.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() fails to find group resources and returns Resource IDs instead of Group IDs
findings.body:
`GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` has three compounding issues:
1. In `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (line 121), individual group resources are created without calling `resource.setType(resourceType)`. Only the all-groups resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` has `type = "Groups"`. Consequently, `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` never finds any per-group resources.
2. Inside the `findByType` callback, `groupResource.getId()` (the internal UUID of the authorization `Resource`) is passed to `hasPermission(...)` and added to `granted`. However, the `GroupModel` ID is stored in `groupResource.getName()`. `hasPermission` looks up the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, so passing `groupResource.getId()` never matches the group resource, and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` returns authorization `Resource` UUIDs instead of group IDs.
3. When an admin has `view-members` or `manage-members` on the all-groups resource, `findByType` matches the all-groups resource and `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns a set containing the all-groups resource UUID. `UsersResource.searchForUser` and `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` then set `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` to that non-existent group ID, causing user searches to return 0 results. Conversely, for per-group `view-members`/`manage-members` permissions, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns an empty set, causing `UsersResource.getUsersCount` (`GET /users/count`) to return 0 and bypassing database-level group filtering during paginated user searches.

findings.title: hasPermission() does not fall back to all-groups resource when a group resource exists for another scope
findings.body: In `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes)`, the all-groups resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`) is only evaluated when `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` returns `null`. If a specific group has a resource created for one scope (e.g., `manage-membership` or `view-members` on `topGroup`) and the caller has a different scope (e.g., `view` or `manage`) granted via an all-groups permission, `resourceStore.findByName(server, topGroup.getId())` returns the `topGroup` resource (`resource != null`). `evaluatePermission` then only evaluates policies attached to `topGroup`, fails to find the `view` or `manage` scope, and returns `false` without checking the all-groups resource.

findings.title: Javadoc on requireManageMembers references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers
findings.body: The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel group)` says `Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}.` It should reference `{@link #canManageMembers(GroupModel)}`.
